title: Yes/No Questions
definition: Yes/no questions are questions that can be answered with ja (yes) or nein (no). In a basic German yes/no question, the conjugated verb comes first, followed by the subject.

rules.title: Basic word order
rules.explanation: Pattern: conjugated verb + subject + the rest of the sentence.

rules.title: Answering yes/no questions
rules.explanation: Answer with ja or nein, and add a short sentence when useful.

examples.german: Kommst du heute? – Ja, ich komme heute.
examples.english: Are you coming today? – Yes, I am coming today.

examples.german: Hast du Zeit? – Nein, ich habe keine Zeit.
examples.english: Do you have time? – No, I don't have time.

rules.title: Questions with haben and sein
rules.explanation: Put the conjugated form of haben or sein at the beginning.

rules.title: Questions with modal verbs
rules.explanation: Put the modal verb first; the main verb stays in the infinitive at the end.

examples.english: Do you have to work today?
Do you want to drink a coffee?

rules.title: Yes/no questions versus W-questions
rules.explanation: Yes/no questions start with the conjugated verb. W-questions start with a question word followed by the conjugated verb.

common_mistakes.explanation: For a standard yes/no question, put the conjugated verb first.
Use the correct conjugated modal verb form.

mastery_goal: You can form and answer basic yes/no questions with regular verbs, sein, haben, and modal verbs.
